meta.description: Structured extraction of the CMA Part 2 Exam Simulator foundational blueprint covering all 6 domains, MCQ/case architecture, certification standards, governance rules, technical architecture, roadmap, and Part 1 vs Part 2 differences.

A.name: Financial Statement Analysis

los_statements.topic: Calculate and interpret financial ratios (5 categories)
Analyze profitability and limitations of ratio analysis
Evaluate ROA, ROE, and earnings quality
Perform comparative financial statement analysis
Evaluate the impact of foreign operations
Assess changing prices and inflation on ratios
Analyze off-balance-sheet financing
Define and analyze operating and financial leverage
Evaluate sustainable growth rate and dividend policy

key_topics: Financial ratio computation and interpretation (liquidity, leverage, activity, profitability, market)
key_formulas: Sustainable Growth Rate = ROE × (1 − Dividend Payout)

B.name: Corporate Finance

los_statements.topic: Calculate risk and return measures (std dev, beta, CAPM)
Calculate cost of capital (WACC, component costs)
Evaluate capital structure and optimal leverage
Manage working capital (cash, receivables, inventory, payables)
Analyze short-term financing and cash management
Evaluate long-term financing (bonds, stocks, leases)
Analyze dividend policy and share repurchases
Assess corporate restructuring (M&A, divestitures, LBOs)
Evaluate international finance (FX, transfer pricing, political risk)

key_topics: Risk and return (std dev, beta, CAPM)
key_formulas: Cash Conversion Cycle = DIO + DSO − DPO

C.name: Decision Analysis

los_statements.topic: Apply CVP analysis (breakeven, target profit, margin of safety)
Perform marginal analysis (special orders, make-or-buy, sell-or-process)
Evaluate pricing decisions (cost-based, market-based, target costing)
Apply relevant costing to short-term decisions
Analyze capacity constraints and product mix
Evaluate business decision models under uncertainty
Assess make-vs-buy and outsourcing decisions

key_formulas: Breakeven (units) = Fixed Costs / CM per Unit
Target Profit (units) = (FC + Target Profit) / CM per Unit
Margin of Safety = (Actual Sales − BE Sales) / Actual Sales
Degree of Operating Leverage = CM / Operating Income
Transfer pricing: Minimum = VC + Opportunity Cost
Perfect Information: EV with PI − EV without PI

D.name: Risk Management

los_statements.topic: Apply COSO ERM framework (governance, strategy, performance, review)
Identify and assess types of risk
Evaluate risk appetite, tolerance, and capacity
Analyze risk response strategies (avoid, reduce, share, accept)
Implement ERM integration with strategy

key_topics: ERM integration with strategy and performance
Types of risk (strategic, operational, financial, hazard)

E.name: Investment Decisions

los_statements.topic: Calculate capital budgeting methods (NPV, IRR, payback, PI, ARR)
Perform DCF analysis for project evaluation
Analyze risk in capital investments (sensitivity, scenario, Monte Carlo)
Evaluate mutually exclusive projects with unequal lives
Define and value real options
Assess post-audit and capital rationing

key_topics: Capital budgeting methods (NPV, IRR, payback, PI, ARR)
key_formulas: Payback = Initial Investment / Annual CF (uniform) or cumulative
Profitability Index = PV of Future CFs / Initial Investment
After-tax cash flow = (Revenue − Expenses) × (1 − t) + (Depreciation × t)

F.name: Professional Ethics

los_statements.topic: Apply IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice
Identify ethical issues facing management accountants
Apply IMA ethical decision-making model
Evaluate fraud and fraudulent financial reporting
Assess corporate governance and ethics (SOX, audit committees)
Apply Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA)
Evaluate sustainability and social responsibility reporting

key_topics: IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice (4 standards)
part2_authorities: IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice

Weighted scoring across blueprint alignment, cognitive level, technical accuracy, distractor quality, business realism, numerical integrity, explanation quality, writing clarity, accessibility, metadata completeness

Scenario requirements, language standards, exhibit standards, cognitive progression, anti-AI writing standards

Independent recalculation, rounding policy, accepted tolerance, formula verification checklist
Difficulty distribution, Bloom's distribution, distractor performance, cueing/bias checks, guessability criteria
Case-level, item-level, exhibit-level metadata schema, validation rules
Technical Review → Psychometric → Numerical → Instructional → Metadata → Final Validation → Approval
MCQ checklist (20 items), case study checklist (additional 12 items)

F: IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice

known_defects.name: Non-empty ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice]
known_defects.mitigation: Governance guard Rule 2 active from first write. QA gate: ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] must be empty string before certification.
known_defects.notes: The highest-frequency structural defect in Part 1. Prevention is critical from Day 1.

known_defects.name: Template boilerplate distractor explanations
known_defects.mitigation: Quality gate: no 'represents a plausible misconception' in any ExplanationWrong field. Distractor explanations must be choice-specific. Pattern match in validator from first batch.
known_defects.notes: Segment 1 boilerplate (exact duplicate generic) is the highest priority. Must not enter the content authoring pipeline.

known_defects.name: Empty non-CorrectChoice ExplanationWrong slots
known_defects.mitigation: Rule 6 (empty distractor BLOCK). All three non-CC ExplanationWrong slots must be non-empty before certification.
known_defects.notes: 1,005 items affected in Part 1. Prevent with automated validator from first item authored.

known_defects.name: Answer-key errors (CorrectChoice disagrees with derived answer)
known_defects.mitigation: Independent recalculation mandatory before certification. Every numerical item must be independently solved by a reviewer who has not seen the stored answer.
known_defects.notes: Five Certified Part 1 items had wrong CorrectChoice. Part 2 must prevent this with mandatory independent recalculation.

known_defects.name: Difficulty inflation (systematic over-labeling)
known_defects.mitigation: Per-item cognitive-level justification required. No template-based difficulty labeling. Each item's difficulty must be justified by its cognitive demand.
known_defects.notes: ~500 Part 1 items labeled Moderate that test Bloom's Remember/Understand. Template-based labeling is the root cause.

known_defects.name: Metadata-content mismatch (dual-block architecture)
known_defects.mitigation: Single-object architecture eliminates this defect class entirely. No separate metadata block and content block per QID.
known_defects.notes: This defect class is architecturally prevented in Part 2. Single-object design means metadata and content are always co-located.

verification_dimensions.name: Correctness
verification_dimensions.description: Against GAAP / IFRS / ICMA CSO / standard managerial accounting
verification_dimensions.requirement: The answer key, explanation, and distractors are consistent with authoritative accounting standards

verification_dimensions.name: Precision
verification_dimensions.requirement: The fact pattern yields exactly one defensible answer; no missing assumptions or contradictory data

verification_dimensions.name: Difficulty Calibration
verification_dimensions.description: Matches stated tier and LOS depth verb
verification_dimensions.requirement: The cognitive demand implied by the LOS is consistent with the question's stated difficulty and Bloom's level

verification_dimensions.name: Distractor Engineering
verification_dimensions.description: Each distractor maps to a real misconception or plausible calculation path
verification_dimensions.requirement: Every distractor represents a documented exam trap or known student error, not a guessable throwaway

verification_dimensions.name: Blueprint Alignment
verification_dimensions.description: Maps to a specific Part 2 CSO LOS
verification_dimensions.requirement: The LOSTag, Topic, and cognitive level align with a specific Content Specification Outline learning outcome

verification_dimensions.name: Part 2 Relevance
verification_dimensions.requirement: The question tests Part 2 material; no concept, standard, or calculation belongs exclusively to Part 1
verification_dimensions.notes: Renamed from CAQS §1.6 Dimension 6 ('CMA Part 1 Relevance'). Explicitly gates against Part 1 content contamination.

auto_fail_conditions: Dimension 3 (Technical Accuracy) score of 0 — item contains a factual error
Dimension 6 (Numerical Integrity) score of 0 — item has wrong numerical answer
Accounting error — correct answer is wrong or explanation contradicts GAAP/COSO/authoritative standards
Numerical error — stored answer does not match correct calculation
Metadata failure — missing required fields that would break the application
Plagiarism — content copied from copyrighted sources
Bias — content that would unfairly disadvantage any candidate group

gold_standard_items.item: Blueprint alignment — Question maps to a specific IMA Learning Outcome Statement
Technical accuracy — Accounting treatment is correct under current GAAP/COSO
Numerical accuracy — All calculations independently verified
Correct answer — The stored CorrectChoice matches expert judgment
Distractor plausibility — Every distractor represents a realistic candidate misconception
Distractor discrimination — No distractor is obviously wrong
No cueing — No grammatical, length, or position cues point to correct answer
Answer balance — Question does not create a pattern if combined with adjacent questions
Explanation principle — Correct answer explanation names the governing standard
Explanation solution — Shows formula with substituted values (calculations) or reasoning chain (conceptual)
Explanation business context — Interprets the result in the scenario
Explanation distractors — Each wrong-choice explanation is specific and teaches why it is wrong
Explanation exam trap — Identifies at least one common candidate error
Business realism — Scenario uses realistic business language, not textbook phrasing
Writing clarity — No grammatical errors; professional tone
Accessibility — No biased language; fair to all candidate populations
Metadata complete — All required fields present and valid
Metadata cross-references — Formula references, trap references, and decision tree references resolve correctly
Validation pass — Automated validation suite passes with zero errors
Review documentation — Audit record exists with scores and findings
Scenario realism — Named company, stakeholder, business trigger, and clear task
Exhibit quality — Professional format, no decorative data
Data consistency — Numbers in exhibits are internally consistent
Question interconnection — Items follow logical progression (calculate → analyze → decide)
Cognitive progression — Items progress from lower to higher Bloom's levels
Independent answerability — Each item can be answered without relying on correct answers to prior items
Exhibit referencing — Every exhibit is referenced by at least one item
Data consumption — Every exhibit row/column is consumed by at least one item
Case-level metadata — All required case-level fields present and valid
Item-level metadata — All required item-level fields present and valid
Exhibit-level metadata — ExhibitID, Purpose, and ReferencedBy fields present
Difficulty calibration — Case-level difficulty is within ±1 of mean item difficulty

certification_blocking_conditions.description: Metadata-block and content-block Choice values diverge — BLOCK certification

CC extraction methodology not using same enclosing object as EW fields — verification invalid
Case item at Apply/Analyze/Evaluate has one-sentence explanation — BLOCK certification
Empty non-CC ExplanationWrong slots — BLOCK certification
